work.title: The First Part of Henry the Sixth
work.author: William Shakespeare

content.text: Enter La Pucelle with four Soldiers with sacks upon their backs.

lines.text: These are the city gates, the gates of Rouen,
lines.plainText: These are the city gates the gates of Rouen

lines.text: Through which our policy must make a breach.
lines.plainText: Through which our policy must make a breach

lines.text: Take heed, be wary how you place your words;
lines.plainText: Take heed be wary how you place your words

lines.text: Talk like the vulgar sort of market men
lines.plainText: Talk like the vulgar sort of market men

lines.text: That come to gather money for their corn.
lines.plainText: That come to gather money for their corn

lines.text: If we have entrance, as I hope we shall,
lines.plainText: If we have entrance as I hope we shall

lines.text: And that we find the slothful watch but weak,
lines.plainText: And that we find the slothful watch but weak

lines.text: I'll by a sign give notice to our friends,
lines.plainText: I'll by a sign give notice to our friends

lines.text: That Charles the Dauphin may encounter them.
lines.plainText: That Charles the Dauphin may encounter them

lines.text: Our sacks shall be a mean to sack the city,
lines.plainText: Our sacks shall be a mean to sack the city

lines.text: And we be lords and rulers over Rouen;
lines.plainText: And we be lords and rulers over Rouen

lines.text: Therefore we'll knock. [Knocks.]
lines.plainText: Therefore we'll knock Knocks

lines.text: [Within.] Qui est la?
lines.plainText: Within Qui est la

lines.text: Paysans, la pauvres gens de France:
lines.plainText: Paysans la pauvres gens de France

lines.text: Poor market folks that come to sell their corn.
lines.plainText: Poor market folks that come to sell their corn

lines.text: Enter, go in; the market bell is rung.
lines.plainText: Enter go in the market bell is rung

lines.text: Now, Rouen, I'll shake thy bulwarks to the ground.
lines.plainText: Now Rouen I'll shake thy bulwarks to the ground

content.text: Enter Charles, the Bastard of Orleans, Alençon, Reignier and forces.

lines.text: Saint Denis bless this happy stratagem,
lines.plainText: Saint Denis bless this happy stratagem

lines.text: And once again we'll sleep secure in Rouen.
lines.plainText: And once again we'll sleep secure in Rouen

lines.text: Here enter'd Pucelle and her practisants;
lines.plainText: Here enter'd Pucelle and her practisants

lines.text: Now she is there, how will she specify
lines.plainText: Now she is there how will she specify

lines.text: Here is the best and safest passage in?
lines.plainText: Here is the best and safest passage in

lines.text: By thrusting out a torch from yonder tower,
lines.plainText: By thrusting out a torch from yonder tower

lines.text: Which, once discern'd, shows that her meaning is:
lines.plainText: Which once discern'd shows that her meaning is

lines.text: No way to that, for weakness, which she enter'd.
lines.plainText: No way to that for weakness which she enter'd

content.text: Enter La Pucelle, on the top, thrusting out a torch burning.

lines.text: Behold, this is the happy wedding torch
lines.plainText: Behold this is the happy wedding torch

lines.text: That joineth Rouen unto her countrymen,
lines.plainText: That joineth Rouen unto her countrymen

lines.text: But burning fatal to the Talbonites.
lines.plainText: But burning fatal to the Talbonites

lines.text: See, noble Charles, the beacon of our friend;
lines.plainText: See noble Charles the beacon of our friend

lines.text: The burning torch, in yonder turret stands.
lines.plainText: The burning torch in yonder turret stands

lines.text: Now shine it like a comet of revenge,
lines.plainText: Now shine it like a comet of revenge

lines.text: A prophet to the fall of all our foes!
lines.plainText: A prophet to the fall of all our foes

lines.text: Defer no time, delays have dangerous ends;
lines.plainText: Defer no time delays have dangerous ends

lines.text: Enter and cry, "The Dauphin!" presently,
lines.plainText: Enter and cry The Dauphin presently

lines.text: And then do execution on the watch.
lines.plainText: And then do execution on the watch

content.text: An alarum. Enter Talbot in an excursion.

lines.text: France, thou shalt rue this treason with thy tears,
lines.plainText: France thou shalt rue this treason with thy tears

lines.text: If Talbot but survive thy treachery.
lines.plainText: If Talbot but survive thy treachery

lines.text: Pucelle, that witch, that damned sorceress,
lines.plainText: Pucelle that witch that damned sorceress

lines.text: Hath wrought this hellish mischief unawares,
lines.plainText: Hath wrought this hellish mischief unawares

lines.text: That hardly we escaped the pride of France.
lines.plainText: That hardly we escaped the pride of France

content.text: An alarum. Excursions. Bedford, brought in sick in a chair. Enter Talbot and Burgundy without: within, La Pucelle, Charles, Bastard, Alençon, and Reignier on the walls.

lines.text: Good morrow, gallants! Want ye corn for bread?
lines.plainText: Good morrow gallants Want ye corn for bread

lines.text: I think the Duke of Burgundy will fast
lines.plainText: I think the Duke of Burgundy will fast

lines.text: Before he'll buy again at such a rate.
lines.plainText: Before he'll buy again at such a rate

lines.text: 'Twas full of darnel. Do you like the taste?
lines.plainText: 'Twas full of darnel Do you like the taste

lines.text: Scoff on, vile fiend and shameless courtezan!
lines.plainText: Scoff on vile fiend and shameless courtezan

lines.text: I trust ere long to choke thee with thine own,
lines.plainText: I trust ere long to choke thee with thine own

lines.text: And make thee curse the harvest of that corn.
lines.plainText: And make thee curse the harvest of that corn

lines.text: Your Grace may starve, perhaps, before that time.
lines.plainText: Your Grace may starve perhaps before that time

lines.text: O, let no words, but deeds, revenge this treason!
lines.plainText: O let no words but deeds revenge this treason

lines.text: What will you do, good graybeard? Break a lance
lines.plainText: What will you do good graybeard Break a lance

lines.text: And run a tilt at Death within a chair?
lines.plainText: And run a tilt at Death within a chair

lines.text: Foul fiend of France and hag of all despite,
lines.plainText: Foul fiend of France and hag of all despite

lines.text: Encompass'd with thy lustful paramours,
lines.plainText: Encompass'd with thy lustful paramours

lines.text: Becomes it thee to taunt his valiant age
lines.plainText: Becomes it thee to taunt his valiant age

lines.text: And twit with cowardice a man half dead?
lines.plainText: And twit with cowardice a man half dead

lines.text: Damsel, I'll have a bout with you again,
lines.plainText: Damsel I'll have a bout with you again

lines.text: Or else let Talbot perish with this shame.
lines.plainText: Or else let Talbot perish with this shame

lines.text: Are ye so hot? Yet, Pucelle, hold thy peace;
lines.plainText: Are ye so hot Yet Pucelle hold thy peace

lines.text: If Talbot do but thunder, rain will follow.
lines.plainText: If Talbot do but thunder rain will follow

lines.text: Dare ye come forth and meet us in the field?
lines.plainText: Dare ye come forth and meet us in the field

lines.text: Belike your lordship takes us then for fools,
lines.plainText: Belike your lordship takes us then for fools

lines.text: To try if that our own be ours or no.
lines.plainText: To try if that our own be ours or no

lines.text: I speak not to that railing Hecate,
lines.plainText: I speak not to that railing Hecate

lines.text: But unto thee, Alençon, and the rest;
lines.plainText: But unto thee Alenon and the rest

lines.text: Will ye, like soldiers, come and fight it out?
lines.plainText: Will ye like soldiers come and fight it out

lines.text: Seignieur, hang! Base muleteers of France!
lines.plainText: Seignieur hang Base muleteers of France

lines.text: Like peasant foot-boys do they keep the walls,
lines.plainText: Like peasant footboys do they keep the walls

lines.text: And dare not take up arms like gentlemen.
lines.plainText: And dare not take up arms like gentlemen

lines.text: Away, captains! Let's get us from the walls,
lines.plainText: Away captains Let's get us from the walls

lines.text: For Talbot means no goodness by his looks.
lines.plainText: For Talbot means no goodness by his looks

lines.text: Goodbye, my lord; we came but to tell you
lines.plainText: Goodbye my lord we came but to tell you

lines.text: That we are here.
lines.plainText: That we are here

lines.text: And there will we be too, ere it be long,
lines.plainText: And there will we be too ere it be long

lines.text: Or else reproach be Talbot's greatest fame!
lines.plainText: Or else reproach be Talbot's greatest fame

lines.text: Vow, Burgundy, by honour of thy house,
lines.plainText: Vow Burgundy by honour of thy house

lines.text: Prick'd on by public wrongs sustain'd in France,
lines.plainText: Prick'd on by public wrongs sustain'd in France

lines.text: Either to get the town again or die.
lines.plainText: Either to get the town again or die

lines.text: And I, as sure as English Henry lives,
lines.plainText: And I as sure as English Henry lives

lines.text: And as his father here was conqueror,
lines.plainText: And as his father here was conqueror

lines.text: As sure as in this late-betrayed town
lines.plainText: As sure as in this latebetrayed town

lines.text: Great Coeur-de-lion's heart was buried,
lines.plainText: Great Coeurdelion's heart was buried

lines.text: So sure I swear to get the town or die.
lines.plainText: So sure I swear to get the town or die

lines.text: My vows are equal partners with thy vows.
lines.plainText: My vows are equal partners with thy vows

lines.text: But, ere we go, regard this dying prince,
lines.plainText: But ere we go regard this dying prince

lines.text: The valiant Duke of Bedford. Come, my lord,
lines.plainText: The valiant Duke of Bedford Come my lord

lines.text: We will bestow you in some better place,
lines.plainText: We will bestow you in some better place

lines.text: Fitter for sickness and for crazy age.
lines.plainText: Fitter for sickness and for crazy age

lines.text: Lord Talbot, do not so dishonour me.
lines.plainText: Lord Talbot do not so dishonour me

lines.text: Here will I sit before the walls of Rouen,
lines.plainText: Here will I sit before the walls of Rouen

lines.text: And will be partner of your weal or woe.
lines.plainText: And will be partner of your weal or woe

lines.text: Courageous Bedford, let us now persuade you.
lines.plainText: Courageous Bedford let us now persuade you

lines.text: Not to be gone from hence; for once I read
lines.plainText: Not to be gone from hence for once I read

lines.text: That stout Pendragon in his litter sick
lines.plainText: That stout Pendragon in his litter sick

lines.text: Came to the field and vanquished his foes.
lines.plainText: Came to the field and vanquished his foes

lines.text: Methinks I should revive the soldiers' hearts,
lines.plainText: Methinks I should revive the soldiers' hearts

lines.text: Because I ever found them as myself.
lines.plainText: Because I ever found them as myself

lines.text: Undaunted spirit in a dying breast!
lines.plainText: Undaunted spirit in a dying breast

lines.text: Then be it so. Heavens keep old Bedford safe!
lines.plainText: Then be it so Heavens keep old Bedford safe

lines.text: And now no more ado, brave Burgundy,
lines.plainText: And now no more ado brave Burgundy

lines.text: But gather we our forces out of hand
lines.plainText: But gather we our forces out of hand

lines.text: And set upon our boasting enemy.
lines.plainText: And set upon our boasting enemy

content.text: An alarum. Excursions. Enter Sir John Fastolf and a Captain.

lines.text: Whither away, Sir John Fastolf, in such haste?
lines.plainText: Whither away Sir John Fastolf in such haste

lines.text: Whither away? To save myself by flight.
lines.plainText: Whither away To save myself by flight

lines.text: We are like to have the overthrow again.
lines.plainText: We are like to have the overthrow again

lines.text: What! Will you fly, and leave Lord Talbot?
lines.plainText: What Will you fly and leave Lord Talbot

lines.text: Ay,
lines.plainText: Ay

lines.text: All the Talbots in the world, to save my life.
lines.plainText: All the Talbots in the world to save my life

lines.text: Cowardly knight, ill fortune follow thee!
lines.plainText: Cowardly knight ill fortune follow thee

content.text: Retreat. Excursions. La Pucelle, Alençon and Charles fly.

lines.text: Now, quiet soul, depart when heaven please,
lines.plainText: Now quiet soul depart when heaven please

lines.text: For I have seen our enemies' overthrow.
lines.plainText: For I have seen our enemies' overthrow

lines.text: What is the trust or strength of foolish man?
lines.plainText: What is the trust or strength of foolish man

lines.text: They that of late were daring with their scoffs
lines.plainText: They that of late were daring with their scoffs

lines.text: Are glad and fain by flight to save themselves.
lines.plainText: Are glad and fain by flight to save themselves

content.text: [Bedford dies, and is carried in by two in his chair.]
An alarum. Enter Talbot, Burgundy and the rest.

lines.text: Lost, and recover'd in a day again!
lines.plainText: Lost and recover'd in a day again

lines.text: This is a double honour, Burgundy.
lines.plainText: This is a double honour Burgundy

lines.text: Yet heavens have glory for this victory!
lines.plainText: Yet heavens have glory for this victory

lines.text: Warlike and martial Talbot, Burgundy
lines.plainText: Warlike and martial Talbot Burgundy

lines.text: Enshrines thee in his heart, and there erects
lines.plainText: Enshrines thee in his heart and there erects

lines.text: Thy noble deeds as valour's monuments.
lines.plainText: Thy noble deeds as valour's monuments

lines.text: Thanks, gentle Duke. But where is Pucelle now?
lines.plainText: Thanks gentle Duke But where is Pucelle now

lines.text: I think her old familiar is asleep.
lines.plainText: I think her old familiar is asleep

lines.text: Now where's the Bastard's braves, and Charles his gleeks?
lines.plainText: Now where's the Bastard's braves and Charles his gleeks

lines.text: What, all amort? Rouen hangs her head for grief
lines.plainText: What all amort Rouen hangs her head for grief

lines.text: That such a valiant company are fled.
lines.plainText: That such a valiant company are fled

lines.text: Now will we take some order in the town,
lines.plainText: Now will we take some order in the town

lines.text: Placing therein some expert officers,
lines.plainText: Placing therein some expert officers

lines.text: And then depart to Paris to the King,
lines.plainText: And then depart to Paris to the King

lines.text: For there young Henry with his nobles lie.
lines.plainText: For there young Henry with his nobles lie

lines.text: What wills Lord Talbot pleaseth Burgundy.
lines.plainText: What wills Lord Talbot pleaseth Burgundy

lines.text: But yet, before we go, let's not forget
lines.plainText: But yet before we go let's not forget

lines.text: The noble Duke of Bedford late deceased,
lines.plainText: The noble Duke of Bedford late deceased

lines.text: But see his exequies fulfill'd in Rouen.
lines.plainText: But see his exequies fulfill'd in Rouen

lines.text: A braver soldier never couched lance,
lines.plainText: A braver soldier never couched lance

lines.text: A gentler heart did never sway in court;
lines.plainText: A gentler heart did never sway in court

lines.text: But kings and mightiest potentates must die,
lines.plainText: But kings and mightiest potentates must die

lines.text: For that's the end of human misery.
lines.plainText: For that's the end of human misery
